$comment: THE ALLOW-LIST OF RULE I1 (milestone SJL-2.1; ADR 0014's admission policy). The only packages any project
of this component's product graph may reference, each with the projects that may reference it.
Each entry names: the package identifier; the pinned version; the NuGet content hash a lock file records
for it (base64 SHA-512 of the .nupkg), which rule I1 compares with the lock file of every project that
references it; the assemblies (by assembly name) of the projects that may reference it, every one in the
JavaScript family, or for a test-only entry a test project; whether it is product or test-only; and its sources under decision SJL-D-4 (c), the
committed feed eng/packages/ and nuget.org once a Broiler.VM package release depends on it.
The list is a file of the architecture-test project, not a field of graph.manifest.json: the manifest
records which project REFERENCES which package (rule A7 holds that to the project files), and this file
records which references are ALLOWED. One answers 'what is', the other 'what may be', and folding the
second into the first would let one edit change both.
Admitting a package is a decision: the milestone or JSD that admits it is named in 'admittedBy', and the
allow-list changes in the same commit as the reference it allows. A test-only package is admitted for no
product project, whatever 'projects' says, and only a test-only entry may name a test project (rule I1 as revised on
2026-10-16, at SJL-7.4, when the owner's generator reached the architecture tests as a pinned, test-only package).
